name: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
summary: AWS managed agent platform composed of modular services — Runtime, Harness, Memory, Gateway, Identity, Policy, Code Interpreter, Observability, and Evaluations — consumed as AWS APIs and usable independently or together. There is no self-hosted distribution.

agent-runtime.note: AgentCore Runtime is a serverless agent runtime with session isolation; AgentCore Harness provides a managed agent loop behind a single API call.

orchestration.note: Harness handles orchestration, tool execution, and multi-step responses; Runtime supports multi-agent workloads including the A2A protocol.

knowledge-memory.note: AgentCore Memory provides short-term multi-turn memory and long-term memory persisting across sessions, with stores shareable across agents.

tools-integration.note: AgentCore Gateway converts APIs and Lambda functions into MCP-compatible tools and connects to existing MCP servers behind a managed endpoint.

identity-governance.note: AgentCore Identity issues workload identities with IdP integration; AgentCore Policy enforces Cedar-based authorization on every Gateway tool call with audit logging.

observability.note: Emits OpenTelemetry traces and CloudWatch dashboards for session count, latency, token usage, and error rates across runtime, memory, gateway, and identity.

data-secrets.note: Identity manages outbound OAuth and API-key credential providers, but durable object storage relies on sibling services such as S3 rather than an AgentCore resource.

evaluation.note: AgentCore Evaluations provides built-in and custom LLM-as-a-judge evaluators with on-demand, batch, online, and dataset runs over agent traces.

channels.note: Agents are exposed through API endpoints only; Slack and similar systems are reachable as outbound Gateway tools, not inbound messaging channels.

code-execution.note: AgentCore Code Interpreter runs agent-generated Python, JavaScript, and TypeScript in an isolated managed sandbox, alongside a managed Browser runtime.

human-in-loop.note: An inline function tool halts the harness mid-run and returns the tool call to the caller, resuming when the client posts a matching tool result on the same session.

multi-tenancy.note: Each runtime session gets an isolated microVM sanitized on termination, but AgentCore does not enforce session-to-user mapping and offers no tenant or namespace resource.

declarative-deployment.note: CloudFormation exposes first-party agent resource types for Runtime, Harness, Gateway, Memory, and Policy, so agent infrastructure is provisioned through stack dependency resolution and change sets.

agent-versioning.note: Every runtime update mints an immutable version; the default endpoint tracks the latest while named endpoints are pinned per environment and moved between versions for staged promotion and rollback.

skill-learning.note: Skills are developer-authored bundles fetched from git, S3, or a catalog, and optimization only produces prompt rewrites a human promotes.
